title: Yu Gwan-sun
summary: Yu Gwan-sun, born in 1902 near Cheonan, entered Ewha Haktang in Seoul in 1915 and took part in the March 1919 independence demonstrations. On 1 April 1919 a protest at Aunae market in her hometown drew about 3,000 people; Japanese military police fired on it, killing 19, including her parents. She was arrested and died in Seodaemun Prison on 28 September 1920, aged 17.

uncertainty.note: Birth: 1902 in the Korea Herald and United Methodist pieces; 16 December 1902 on the Historical Parallax page. Age at death is 17 by Western reckoning or 18 by Korean reckoning (Parallax).

importance.justification: Sources record her role in the March 1919 independence movement, the Aunae market protest where 19 were killed, and her death in prison aged 17.

audience_note: Describes the shooting of protesters, including the subject's parents, and the death of a teenager in prison custody.

reviewer_note: Aunae market is placed in her hometown by the Korea Herald; the Parallax page contradicts itself about Aunae vs Byeongcheon market, so the pin is the Byeongcheon locality (about 6 km). Place of death is Seodaemun Prison per Parallax; the Korea Herald says only that she was held there. Prison is named but the pin is Byeongcheon.
